ENG.name: Engagement with a thinker across texts
ENG.map_contract: G5 companion, not a revision of citation_invocation_map v2
ENG.question: How does this author use and read this thinker across the supplied citing texts?
ENG.ideal: A bibliographic reading of A on P, led by P's place in these arguments. Give a passage × cited object × move × stance × reading × locus table, then a text/year trajectory table. Distinguish evidence, foil and dialogue; pair the actual passages before claiming development. Give a scholar three to five passages to open first and say why.

dimensions.name: The thinker's place in this argument
questions: What does this text argue, and what place does the named thinker have in that argument?
dimensions.method_card: Do: Read the whole citing text for its argument and P's role. A quoted reader's position is not automatically A's. On a secondary or primary-work document report outside scope. Select literal spans that carry the actor, predicate, object and necessary qualification. A name or topic alone cannot support a reading. Use separate anchor-b/doc-b for a second span; never stitch quotations. Keep attribution, negation, modality, edition and chronology. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.

steps.reader: a scholar of A with the cited works and secondary texts open
steps.brief:

G6.name: Citation fidelity audit
G6.question: Does each attribution hold against the supplied page window of the work it cites?
G6.ideal: A paired audit of the evidence index: for every indexed attribution, A's actual claim and anchor beside P's own words and anchor, attribution kind, accurate/fair/selective/stretched/misattributed/unverifiable verdict with a reason, and edition/locus notes. State how many pairs and works were checked, unresolved and outside the sample. A practice conclusion applies only to the checked sample.

dimensions.name: Who attributes what to whom
questions: Does A directly attribute a claim to P, report P reporting another view, contrast P with another, or merely name P?
dimensions.method_card: Do: Work from the A side of each indexed pair. Preserve nested attribution. A mere mention makes no substantive attribution to audit. In a W-only document defer A-side conclusions until the paired comparison. Select literal spans that carry the actor, predicate, object and necessary qualification. A name or topic alone cannot support a reading. Use separate anchor-b/doc-b for a second span; never stitch quotations. Keep attribution, negation, modality, edition and chronology. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.

dimensions.name: A's actual attribution
questions: What exactly does A attribute at this citation, in A's own terms and with A's qualification?
dimensions.method_card: Do: Copy the supporting A clause; retain quotation versus paraphrase and creative adaptation versus a claim to literal fidelity. In a footnote pair, read the body sentence to which the note belongs. Do not use an index's generated description as A's words. Select literal spans that carry the actor, predicate, object and necessary qualification. A name or topic alone cannot support a reading. Use separate anchor-b/doc-b for a second span; never stitch quotations. Keep attribution, negation, modality, edition and chronology. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.

dimensions.name: P's own position at the retrieved place
questions: What does P say in the held page window, and whose voice is speaking there?
dimensions.method_card: Do: Read only the W side. Copy P's own words verbatim. A translator's introduction, editorial note, table of contents or quoted opponent is not P's assertion. If nothing here settles the attribution, report that limit rather than recalling P's work. Select literal spans that carry the actor, predicate, object and necessary qualification. A name or topic alone cannot support a reading. Use separate anchor-b/doc-b for a second span; never stitch quotations. Keep attribution, negation, modality, edition and chronology. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.

dimensions.name: Verdict on each supplied pair
questions: Does A's attribution hold against P's own words in this retrieved window: accurate, fair, selective, stretched, misattributed or unverifiable, and why?
dimensions.method_card: Do: Pair an anchor from the actual A text with anchor-b from the actual W window, using distinct supplied document keys. These are corpus rows because the verdict predicates a relation between two sources, even though the unit is one citation. Stretched or misattributed requires P's own contrary words; otherwise say unverifiable. Search-window irrelevance warrants unverifiable, not misattributed. Keep every index ID accounted for in the audit table, even when no positive verdict is possible. Select literal spans that carry the actor, predicate, object and necessary qualification. A name or topic alone cannot support a reading. Use separate anchor-b/doc-b for a second span; never stitch quotations. Keep attribution, negation, modality, edition and chronology. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.

dimensions.name: Practice across the checked sample

dimensions.method_card: Do: Count checked pair IDs once; do not count multiple findings or overlapping windows as independent citations. Re-anchor, narrow or reject a claim whose quotation omits its predicate. Code checks only anchors and IDs; the model must judge the reading against the supplied text.
